statement: KTM's 2025 450 SX-F repair manual lists a service schedule with columns After 1 operating hour, Every 15, Every 45 and Every 90 operating hours and every 24 months, with valve clearance checked after 1 h then every 45 h, fork and shock service every 45 h, minor engine service every 45 h and major engine service every 90 h.

rows.task: Check the chain, rear sprocket, engine sprocket, and chain guide.
Grease all moving parts (e.g., hand lever, chain,...) and check for smooth operation.
Change the spark plug and spark plug connector.
Clean the air filter and air filter box.
Change the glass fiber filling of the main silencer.
Check all screws, nuts, and hose clips for a tight fit.
Check the antifreeze and coolant level.
Check the steering head bearing for play.

Perform minor engine service including removing and installing the engine (change the piston, check/measure the cylinder, check the cylinder head, check the camshafts and valve train system components, check the timing assembly, change the radial shaft seal rings of the water pump, change the crankshaft seal ring, change the intake flange, change inlet sleeve).

Perform major engine service, engine is removed (change valves, valve springs, valve spring seats and valve spring retainer; change the connecting rod, conrod bearing and crank pin; check the transmission and the shift mechanism; check the oil pressure control valve; change the suction pump; check the force pump and lubrication system; change the timing chain; change all engine bearings and all gaskets; change the freewheel).
Final check: check vehicle for operating safety.
Read out the fault memory using the KTM diagnostics tool after a test ride.
Enter electronic proof of service in the dealer portal.

notes: Chapter 29. The 'After 1 operating hour' column is a one-time check (open circles); all other marks are periodic. Engine-service row text lightly condensed.

statement: KTM's 2025 450 SX-F repair manual lists valve clearance as 0.10-0.15 mm intake and 0.12-0.17 mm exhaust measured cold at 20 °C (68 °F), set by swapping shims under the rocker arms after the timing chain tensioner and camshaft have been removed.

steps_summary: Prep: on FACTORY EDITION and XC-F US remove the engine guard; remove the seat and fuel tank (engine can stay in the frame).

Measure first: pull the spark plug, remove the valve cover and the stator-cover screw plug, rotate the crank counterclockwise to TDC (camshaft LOCK mark aligned with the retaining bracket) and lock it with the locking screw.
With a feeler gauge, measure every valve between valve and rocker arm and note the readings.
If out of spec, check the rocker arm rollers first: no radial play is allowed; replace a rocker arm with play before adjusting.
Remove the timing chain tensioner and camshaft (per the cylinder-head removal section) so the rocker arms can be lifted.
Lift each rocker arm outward and take out the shims, keeping them in their installed positions.
Work out the corrected shim thickness from the measured clearance and fit suitable shims.
Reassemble, then re-check the clearance on all valves.
Refit fuel tank, seat and (FACTORY EDITION / XC-F US) engine guard.
vals.check_interval: After 1 operating hour (one-time), then every 45 operating hours (service schedule)

notes: Paraphrased summary. Clearances from section 26.1, measuring steps and special tools from 23.1, torques from the 26.3 engine torque table. Shim selection and the step-by-step camshaft/tensioner torque sequence are not summarised here; follow the manual.
